overview.text:
**Changed**
- `index.js:unescapeHtml` (new) runs `('' + string).replace(matchEntityRegExp, …)` and maps `" & < >` to `" & < >` [E5, H5].
- Numeric refs (`&#NNN;` and `&#xHH;`/`&#XHH;`) go through `parseInt`, and `'` takes this decimal path [H3, H5].
- Code points above `0x10FFFF` or in `0xD800–0xDFFF` return the original entity. Others are returned via `String.fromCharCode`, with surrogate pairs above `0xFFFF` [H5].
- The regex `matchEntityRegExp` requires a trailing `;` and matches only lowercase named entities. Unknown or malformed entities are left as-is [H3].
- `index.js` adds the export `module.exports.unescape = unescapeHtml`. The default `escapeHtml` export is unchanged [H4].
- `README.md` rewrites the intro sentence and adds an `### escapeHtml.unescape(string)` section with an example [H1, H2].

**Why**
- The user asked for a dependency-free inverse of `escapeHtml` with numeric reference support, safe handling of invalid code points, node:test tests and README docs [E1].
- The agent first checked how `escapeHtml` is exported, then attached `unescape` as a function property [E2, E4, H4].
- The agent stated no other reasons for its design choices (one decoding layer per call, surrogate rejection) [E9].

**Tests**
- New file `test/unescape.test.js` contains 10 tests [H6]:
  - Export types, plus a round trip `unescape(escapeHtml(original)) === original` [H6].
  - Decimal refs, including leading zeros (`<`) [H6].
  - Hex refs with mixed `x`/`X` prefix and letter case [H6].
  - Emoji/supplementary characters and boundaries `�`, `퟿`, ``, ``, `𐀀`, `` [H6].
  - Invalid refs left unchanged: `�`, surrogates, and huge digit strings [H6].
  - Unknown or uppercase names (`©`, `&`, `&constructor;`) left unchanged [H6].
  - Unterminated or malformed refs (`&quot`, `&#;`, `&#-1;`, `&#xGG;`) left unchanged [H6].
  - Single-layer decoding: `&lt;` becomes `<` [H6].
  - Coercion of `undefined`, `null`, `42`, `{}`, and a custom `toString` [H6].
- `node --test test/unescape.test.js` exited 0 with 10 passing [E5, E9].
- `npm test` exited 127 with `mocha: not found` [E6].
- The existing `test/index.js` passed 30/30 through a `node -e` shim mapping `describe`/`it` to node:test [E8].

**Risks**
- The real mocha suite was never run, so the shim is the only check on the existing tests [E6, E8].
- `�` and C1 control code points are decoded to raw characters, not U+FFFD as the HTML spec would map them. The `�` behaviour is asserted in a test [H5, H6].
- The README intro was reworded, which goes beyond adding a new section [H1].
- An earlier exploration command exited 1 (the `rg` search for `AGENTS.md`). Its effect on the session is not shown [E4].

walkthrough.text:

2. **Explore:** Read `index.js` and saw `module.exports = escapeHtml` with a `matchHtmlRegExp = /["'&<>]/` switch-based escaper. [E4]
3. **Explore, failure:** The second command (`cat README.md && cat test/index.js && rg --files -g AGENTS.md`) exited 1. The cause is not shown; likely `rg` found no `AGENTS.md`. The agent did not react to it. [E4]
4. **Edit:** Added `matchEntityRegExp = /&(?:quot|amp|lt|gt|#([0-9]+)|#[xX]([0-9a-fA-F]+));/g`. `'` is handled by the decimal branch. [E5, H3]
5. **Edit:** Exported `module.exports.unescape = unescapeHtml`. [E5, H4]
6. **Edit:** In `unescapeHtml`, input is coerced with `'' + string`, then `.replace`. Named entities map through a `switch`; numeric references go through `parseInt` (base 10 or 16). [E5, H5]
7. **Edit:** Code points above `0x10FFFF` or in `0xD800`–`0xDFFF` return the original entity. Values up to `0xFFFF` use `fromCharCode`; higher values are built as a manual surrogate pair. [H5]
8. **Edit:** Created `test/unescape.test.js` with 10 `node:test` cases. They cover round-trip, decimal/hex, supplementary characters, invalid code points, unknown/cased entities, malformed references, single-layer decoding and coercion. [E5, H6]
9. **Edit:** Rewrote the README intro and added an `escapeHtml.unescape(string)` section with rules and an example. [E5, H1, H2]
10. **Test:** `node --test test/unescape.test.js` exited 0. The agent reports 10 passing; the output is truncated. [E5, E7]
11. **Test:** `git diff --check` was clean. The diff stat showed `README.md` and `index.js` modified, plus an untracked test file. [E6]
12. **Test, failure:** `npm test` exited 127 with `sh: 1: mocha: not found`. [E6]
13. **Fix:** The agent worked around this by running `test/index.js` with `node:test`'s `describe`/`it` assigned to globals. 30 tests passed, 0 failed. [E7, E8]
14. **Report:** Summarized the 10 new tests passing, the 30 existing tests passing via the shim, and `npm test` being unavailable. [E9]
15. **Not verified:** The suite was never run under real Mocha via `npm test`. `benchmark/index.js` and `component.json` were not updated or checked (not shown). [E6, E9]

mechanism.text:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["unescape(string) = module.exports.unescape [H4]"] --> B["coerce: '' + string [H5]"]
  B --> C["str.replace(matchEntityRegExp, callback) [H3, H5]"]
  C -->|"no regex match: unknown or malformed entity [H3, H6]"| D["text left unchanged"]
  C -->|"match: entity, decimal, hex [H5]"| E["switch on entity"]
  E -->|"" & < > [H5]"| F["return literal char"]
  E -->|"numeric reference [H5]"| G["codePoint = parseInt(decimal,10) or parseInt(hex,16)"]
  G -->|"> 0x10FFFF or 0xD800..0xDFFF [H5]"| H["return original entity"]
  G -->|"<= 0xFFFF [H5]"| I["String.fromCharCode(codePoint)"]
  G -->|"0x10000..0x10FFFF [H5]"| J["surrogate pair: 0xD800+(cp>>10), 0xDC00+(cp&0x3FF)"]
  F --> K["decoded string, one layer [H2, H6]"]
  H --> K
  I --> K
  J --> K
  D --> K
```

The diagram is derived from `matchEntityRegExp`, the export line and `unescapeHtml` [H3, H4, H5].

- `escapeHtml` is still the default export. `unescape` is attached as a property: `module.exports.unescape = unescapeHtml` [H4]. Test 1 checks both exports are functions [H6, E5].
- Input is coerced with `'' + string`, the same as `escapeHtml` [H5]. The test passes `undefined`, `null`, `42`, `{}` and a custom `toString` returning `<` (which becomes `<`) [H6].
- `matchEntityRegExp` is global and matches only these forms, each ending in `;` [H3]:
  - `"`, `&`, `<`, `>` [H3]
  - `&#digits;`, capturing group 1 [H3]
  - `&#x`/`&#X` hex, capturing group 2 [H3]
- Text the regex doesn't match never reaches the callback, so it stays as-is [H3, H5]:
  - Unknown or wrongly cased names: `©`, `'`, `&`, `&constructor;` [H6]
  - Missing semicolons or bad digits: `&quot `, `&#;`, `&#-1;`, `&#12a;`, `&#xGG;` [H3, H6]
- The `switch` has cases for the four named entities only [H5]. `'` has no named case. It goes through the decimal path, which the "decodes all entities emitted by escapeHtml" round-trip test covers [H5, H6].
- `parseInt` turns the captured digits into a number, with radix 10 or 16 [H5]. Huge inputs such as 40 nines or `&#xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF;` produce numbers above `0x10FFFF`. They go to the "leave unchanged" branch, so nothing throws [H5, H6].
- The invalid-range check (`> 0x10FFFF`, or within `0xD800`–`0xDFFF`) returns the original entity text [H5]. Tests cover:
  - `�` and `�` [H6]
  - `�`, `�`, `�`, `�` [H5, H6]
- Code points up to `0xFFFF` go through `String.fromCharCode`. Tests cover `�`, `퟿`, ``, ``, leading zeros in `<`, and mixed-case `<` [H5, H6].
- Supplementary code points are converted to a surrogate pair by hand, not with `String.fromCodePoint` [H5]. Tests cover `😀`/`😀` (both 😀), `𐀀` and `` [H6].
- A single `replace` pass decodes one layer only: `&lt;` becomes `<`, not `<`. This is tested and documented [H2, H6].
- Verification results [E5, E6, E8]:
  - `node --test test/unescape.test.js` exited 0; the agent reports 10 passing tests [E5, E7].
  - The existing `test/index.js` suite passed 30/30 using `node:test` shims for `describe`/`it` [E8].
  - `npm test` failed with exit 127 because `mocha` isn't installed [E6].
